headline: Powell's Jackson Hole speech triggers rally; September rate-cut odds top 90%
summary: Fed Chair Powell said Friday that 'the baseline outlook and the shifting balance of risks may warrant adjusting our policy stance,' widely read as opening the door to a September cut. CME FedWatch odds of a Sept 17 cut jumped past 90%. Equities ripped: S&P 500 +1.5% to close the week, Nasdaq +1.9%, Dow +846 pts. Long-end Treasury yields fell. Sets a supportive macro backdrop for AI-infra and duration-sensitive nuclear/utility trades (CEG, VST, NEE, OKLO, SMR) into a week dominated by NVDA earnings Wednesday.

headline: Samsung Electronics unveils record W110tr (~$80B) shareholder return; buyback starts today
summary: Samsung's board approved a 2026 shareholder-return package of KRW 90–110 trillion (~$66–80B), the largest ever by a Korean company and more than 5x its prior 2020 record of W20.3tr. Plan includes ~W30tr in Q3 cash dividends and an open-market repurchase of 53.3M common shares from Aug 24 through Nov 21 (~W15tr) for employee compensation; remainder to be decided at Jan board meeting. KOSPI opened -1.4% Monday with 005930.KS -6% as investors debated whether the payout ratio (~50% of FCF) signals confidence or a slowing internal reinvestment runway for HBM/foundry capex. Near-term overhang for the stock; medium-term positive for capital discipline.

headline: Broadcom's AI-financing debt package now sized above $70B, per CNBC sources
summary: Follow-up reporting on the Broadcom/Apollo/Blackstone AI-debt structure (initially reported Aug 20 at ~$60B) says the senior tranche alone is now expected to reach north of $70B, with total commitments potentially at $100B when a ~$30B junior tranche is added. Proceeds bankroll custom silicon (XPU/networking) capacity for Anthropic, OpenAI, and other hyperscalers ordering off Broadcom's Jericho/Tomahawk roadmap. Signals both AI-capex durability and the growing off-balance-sheet financing plumbing behind it — bullish AVGO, cascading positive for TSM/AMAT/LRCX/KLAC and HBM (MU, 000660.KS, 005930.KS).

headline: Anthropic files confidential S-1 targeting October IPO at ~$2T valuation; ARR hits $65B
summary: Anthropic confidentially filed with the SEC for an IPO reportedly as soon as October at a valuation approaching $2T, more than double its most recent $965B Series H mark. Company disclosed $65B ARR in July (up from $47B in May), passing OpenAI's ~$40B run-rate. Filing formalizes what has been the fastest revenue ramp ever seen in software; the read-through is more capex, more compute, more compute-adjacent power. Direct positives: NVDA, AVGO (custom Claude accelerator program), TSM, VRT, ETN, GEV, CEG.

headline: SK Hynix showcases CPO + custom-HBM + memory-pooling roadmap at TSMC Technology Symposium
summary: At TSMC's Silicon Valley Technology Symposium (Aug 22 local), SK Hynix reaffirmed its partnership with TSMC and outlined a roadmap that combines Co-Packaged Optics (CPO), custom HBM (base-die on TSMC logic nodes), and memory-pooling to attack the AI accelerator bandwidth wall. HBM4 mass production is on track for 2H26; base-die integration on TSMC N3/N2 lets customers (NVDA, AMD, GOOGL TPU, custom silicon) buy application-tuned HBM stacks. Reinforces SK Hynix's ~50–55% HBM share lead vs Samsung and Micron. Positive for 000660.KS, TSM; competitive pressure on 005930.KS to close the gap.

headline: Samsung accelerates Taylor, TX second fab build; equipment partners asked to begin tool cert
summary: Samsung has quietly asked key semiconductor equipment vendors — reportedly AMAT, LRCX, KLAC, and TEL — to begin certifications required to install tools at the second Taylor, Texas fab, ahead of the previously communicated schedule. Consistent with prior signals that Samsung wants to convert Taylor into a real 2nm foundry footprint and win Qualcomm/Tesla/AMD volume. Incrementally positive for US semi-equip WFE order books in 2026–27; supports Lam's constructive commentary that 2026 WFE is tracking toward the low $150B range vs. the prior $140B guide.

headline: Monday setup: US futures higher on Powell tailwind; Asian tech weak; NVDA earnings Wednesday is the week's swing factor
summary: S&P e-minis +0.4% and Nasdaq-100 futures +0.3% pre-open Monday as the Jackson Hole dovish read holds. Asia was heavier: MSCI Asia-Pac -0.2% with tech leading declines, Kospi -1.4% dragged by Samsung -6% on the capital-return news. Focus for the week: NVDA fiscal Q2 (Wed Aug 26 AMC) with buy-side whisper $95–98B revenue vs. Street $93–95B and company guide $91B ±2%; also CRM/CRWD/OKTA/VEEV that same day. Follow-ons include MRVL after the close Thursday. Setup favors AI-infra bulls if NVDA reprints the beat/raise pattern; a soft data-center print risks a broader AI-capex reset given rich positioning.

headline: Trump 15% polysilicon tariff takes effect; adds cost pressure on solar, tilts new datacenter power mix further toward gas & nuclear
summary: A 15% ad-valorem tariff plus minimum-import-price floor on polysilicon and certain derivatives kicked in this month under Presidential Proclamation. Directly raises US utility-scale solar module cost; at the margin, this reinforces the observed shift in new datacenter power deals toward firm gas (GEV turbine backlog) and nuclear (CEG, VST, existing SMR options with OKLO/SMR). Neutral-to-negative for AES/NEE renewable pipeline economics; incremental positive for gas-turbine/BOP suppliers (GEV, ETN, VRT) and reactor operators.
